quality.notes: rewrite_action_items passes the same bound set to every item, and ActionItem::Let never adds its name. Thus a later Expr::Var colliding with component state or const is qualified. The mechanism is actionable, although the available source does not establish whether such shadowing is legal or how Let scope is intended.

The asymmetry is real, but the claimed defect assumes a ForAll binder is an assignable local. The source instead consistently treats LValue variable names as state targets while bound names affect expressions; assigning component state x using binder x is therefore a plausible intended interpretation. Quantified and Aggregate expressions cannot contain statement lvalues.

No existing fall-through Expr or TypeExpr variant carrying a rewritable identifier is identified. The explicit arms cover recursive forms, while the catch-all plausibly preserves leaf and already-global forms; hypothetical future variants are not a current actionable defect. ComponentNames also contains no callable-function namespace supporting qualification of Expr::Call names.
